The CCW this fact needs (Marshal.GetComInterfaceForObject) is a Windows COM facility, so the subscription cannot be exercised elsewhere. The non-Windows arm is NOT silent: WindowsOrTypedUnsupported() asserts the product's typed unsupported-platform refusal and its detail text before returning, so every supported OS lands in an asserting arm. The deny DECISION carries no such predicate at all - it was extracted into WebViewPermissionDeny.AnswerRequest (pure vtable traffic, no CCW) precisely so the eight TheAnswer_* facts in this file run on every platform, which took this file from twelve shaped sites to three

Same Windows-CCW precondition and the same asserting non-Windows arm as the entry above. This is the fact that proves the pointer handed to slot 23 is the handler that denies - it invokes that CCW through its own vtable and observes DENY arrive at put_State - so it cannot be expressed without the CCW it needs. The deny DECISION it corroborates is asserted platform-independently by the eight TheAnswer_* facts, which drive WebViewPermissionDeny.AnswerRequest (pure vtable traffic, no CCW) and carry no platform predicate at all

Same Windows-CCW precondition and the same asserting non-Windows arm as the two entries above. Detach can only be exercised on a subscription that exists, and the subscription needs the CCW; making it cross-platform by reflecting the signal's internal constructor was possible and was REJECTED, because a token this fact invented rather than received would make Assert.Equal(DefaultToken, remove.TokenSeen) tautological and lose the attach-to-detach round trip. The deny decision itself needs no CCW and is asserted everywhere by the eight TheAnswer_* facts over WebViewPermissionDeny.AnswerRequest

not-vacuous: exhaustive platform arms over a TYPED REFUSAL CODE, with no skip and no early return. Every backend checks the MECHANISM before it checks whether anything is presented, so the same call answers nothing-presented on Windows and mechanism-absent off it; both are refusals, both are true of their platform, and NEITHER arm is a success. The platform predicate selects the EXPECTED CODE and guards no assertion - the fact executes end to end on every platform, which is why it is NOT in allowedSkips.

OS gate, not a silenced assertion: the fact drives a REAL Win32 rig (a layered surface through USER32, a Media Foundation decode, a SendInput click, or a card that takes the foreground), and off Windows there is no rig to read - several of its readings would not merely be absent but WRONG, because every handle is 0 and a winner == window comparison is then 0 == 0 about a window that does not exist. The gate is Assert.SkipUnless rather than an early return, so the skip REPORTS, and it is pinned by NAME in floor.json allowedSkips under the admission rule (an OS property, not satisfiable by configuration; machine class named there). Every assertion below the gate is unchanged and runs in full on Windows, and the skip reason names the fact that asserts the off-Windows answer instead.
